title: [YouPass Collect] - Population Growth in 3 Major Cities
prompt: The chart shows information about the actual and expected figures of population of three cities, Jakarta, Sao Paulo, and Shanghai. Summarize the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.

frame.name: Introduction
paragraphs: The bar chart compares the actual population of three cities, which are Jakarta, Shanghai, and Sao Paulo, in 1990 and 2000, alongside the projected figures for the year 2000.

frame.name: Overview
paragraphs: Overall, all three cities experienced population growth between 1990 and 2000, with the actual figures surpassing the predictions in every case. Additionally, Sao Paulo remained the most populous city throughout the period, while Jakarta was consistently the smallest.

frame.name: Body 1
paragraphs: Starting with the largest city, Sao Paulo had a population of 17 million in 1990, which was 5 million more than Shanghai and over double that of Jakarta. By 2000, while demographic projections estimated its population would reach around 21.5 million, the actual figure climbed to 24 million, representing an increase of approximately 7 million, or roughly 41%, over the decade. This meant the actual population exceeded forecasts by 2.5 million residents.

frame.name: Body 2
paragraphs: Regarding the smaller cities, Shanghai and Jakarta recorded respective populations of 12 million and 8 million in 1990, with the former being 50% larger than the latter. Interestingly, Shanghai's population was predicted to decline marginally to 11 million by 2000; however, it actually surged to 15 million, a 25% increase from 1990 and a dramatic 4 million above predictions. Similarly, Jakarta's population expanded from 8 million to 12.5 million in 2000, which was 1.5 million higher than the projected 11 million, marking a growth of approximately 56% from its 1990 baseline.
